Understanding equipment maintenance in your setting

You should:

understand what equipment is used in your care setting to support individuals’ care needs

understand who provides and is responsible for the maintenance of the care equipment used in your setting

be able to inspect and maintain the equipment that is your responsibility within your care setting, ensuring that it is safe for use when maintenance has been completed

understand that individuals’ safety is paramount and that all equipment should be maintained in way that protects their safety

understand the limits of your knowledge and when you may need to contact external support for the maintenance of equipment in your setting

be able to support communication with external agencies or providers who may be responsible for the inspection and maintenance of equipment in your setting

be able to ensure that external providers also maintain individuals’ dignity and rights while equipment maintenance work is being carried out

ensure that equipment is inspected and maintained within your setting

Understanding maintenance in your setting

You should:

understand what maintenance needs to be undertaken in your setting

understand what inspections your setting might need, and their frequency, to ensure the safety and wellbeing of individuals (for example, gas safety checks, hot water and boiler checks)

be able to undertake maintenance of the setting. This may include:

fixing plumbing and electrical issues

fitting and repair of fixtures, fittings and furniture

other minor carpentry works

painting and other decorating

maintaining the grounds of the setting

be able to ensure that heating is checked regularly and seasonally adjusted, set to a temperature that is safe and comfortable for people who draw on care and support

be able to help ensure that utilities in your setting are consistent and safe to use. This might include:

ensuring that internet access is working and consistent in your setting

ensuring that water temperature is safe for individuals to use

ensuring that electricity is consistent and that it is safe to use (for example, making sure wiring is not damaged or exposed)

be able to recognise emergencies, like boiler breakdowns, and how these emergencies might cause more harm in an adult social care environment

be able to mitigate and manage these risks, ensuring that individuals’ safety is paramount

where your service uses vehicles, ensure they are kept safe and well maintained for use, including ensuring they meet safety standards for transporting people who draw on care and support

understand when these vehicles need to be serviced and inspected (MOT or otherwise) and ensure these inspections and servicing are undertaken within the appropriate timeframes

understand the need for portable appliance testing (PAT) of wired equipment in adult social care settings

be able to ensure that all wired equipment is PAT tested in your setting, including equipment that is brought in externally by individuals, their families or by external contractors or providers

Health and safety

You should:

understand and ensure the implementation of health and safety policy and emergency and fire procedures

ensure that all equipment and tools are stored safely so they are not a hazard

ensure that control of substances hazardous to health (COSHH) regulations are adhered to in your work

be able to monitor that all entrances and fire exits are kept free of obstructions

ensure all incidents and accidents are recorded and reported according to your organisation’s policy

be able to implement any risk management actions as instructed

be able to support with risk assessments relating to health and safety in your setting

be able to recognise hazards and help mitigate or eliminate these in your setting

ensure waste is managed and disposed of safely, particularly recognising the hazardous waste generated in care settings

ensure that fire safety checks are undertaken and appropriately recorded in your setting

ensure that any security systems are inspected and maintained in your setting

where relevant, ensure that the setting is inspected for asbestos and that there is an up-to-date asbestos survey and management plan

be able to regularly check the setting for any hazards that might cause trips or falls, and work to ensure these hazards are eliminated

Engaging with IT systems

You should:

be able to record maintenance in IT systems as directed by your organisation

be able to keep up-to-date and accurate records of maintenance work in your setting

be able to keep records of service contracts and inspection reports and timings

be able to support inspection processes as directed by the management in your setting

understand the budget available to you for maintenance

be able to track maintenance budgets through systems agreed with your employer

understand when works may exceed the budget provided to you and the method by which you can request additional funds for maintenance, to keep your setting safe, secure and well maintained for individuals

Understanding person-centred care

You should:

understand what is meant by the term ‘person-centred care’

understand how you can support the provision of person-centred care in your setting

be able to positively engage with people who draw on care and support, supporting them to have a positive experience with adult social care

Support individuals’ health and wellbeing

You should be able to support the health and wellbeing of people who draw on care and support.

Additional knowledge and skills
